html:
Takla is the homeland of the Takla Lake First Nation, a Dakelh (Carrier) and Sekani people of the northern interior of British Columbia, around Takla Lake and the upper Omineca country. Their languages are Athabaskan.

They lived by hunting, trapping and fishing for salmon and lake fish, and traded furs with the North West Company and the Hudson's Bay Company from the early 1800s. The present First Nation was formed in the mid 1900s from the merger of smaller bands. Their neighbours include the Tsek'ehne (Sekani) and the Yekooche.
